rating.actual_role: Documentation generator rendering a reflected type into Markdown with declaration, inheritance, constructors, fields, properties, and methods.
rating.hardest_behavior: A declaration-rendering change needs a focused check of reflected type categories: suppress enum inheritance text, distinguish static from abstract classes without treating interfaces the same way, and preserve indexer parameter formatting. These are localized presentation assumptions rather than a stateful algorithm.
rating.counterevidence: Most of the body independently emits a section if its prepared member collection is nonempty. Metadata gathering and ordering are performed by TypeInfo, and naming/summary formatting is delegated to helpers. There is no backtracking, transactional state, or interaction among the member sections beyond appending output.
rating.inspection_scope: Read TypeGenerator.cs completely (1-118) and its TypeInfo.cs metadata builder completely (1-93). Did not execute the generator or inspect all naming-extension implementations.

evidence.observation: Declaration rendering locally combines enum inheritance suppression with mutually exclusive static/abstract modifiers based on reflection flags.
Inheritance, constructors, and fields are emitted as independent sections from prepared collections; these repeated presentation loops do not create coupled state.
Property rendering has one localized distinction for indexers, formatting their parameter types instead of the ordinary property name.
Method rendering directly appends names and summaries from the prepared method list, with no additional selection or lifecycle logic.

rating.role: Public exception data carrier for a malformed CSV field and its raw record.

rating.counterevidence: The type is a public serializable exception, so compatibility still matters, but no custom serialization, parsing, or state transitions are implemented here.
rating.inspection_scope: Read entire assigned BadDataException.cs, lines 1-64; no additional context.

evidence.observation: The exception adds two readonly strings describing the original field and row.
The basic constructor forwards context and directly assigns both payload fields.
The message and inner-exception overloads use the same direct payload assignments with corresponding base-constructor forwarding.

rating.role: Production shared CSV context and facade for configuration, converter caches, and class-map registration.
rating.hardest_behavior: Keeping each constructor associated with the correct reader/parser/writer configuration and applying registration validation before adding maps. A change mainly requires focused checking of overload delegation and which operations mutate the map collection.
rating.counterevidence: Automapping, resolution, and map-collection behavior are delegated to other components. This file exposes shared state but does not itself coordinate a multistep parsing lifecycle or implement mapping recursion.
rating.inspection_scope: Read entire assigned CsvContext.cs, lines 1-196. Related assigned ObjectRecordCreator.cs and its inspected RecordCreator/ExpressionManager context also show consumption of this context; ClassMapCollection internals were not inspected.

evidence.observation: Constructors select their source component's CsvConfiguration and allocate a ClassMapCollection bound to this context; reader construction also captures its parser.
Generic/type registration resolves an instance then delegates to map registration, which rejects maps having no member, reference, or parameter mappings.
Both AutoMap overloads create and populate a default map and immediately add it to Maps before returning it.

rating.role: Production factory compiling typed record-construction delegates from CSV class maps.
rating.hardest_behavior: Changing how a map becomes a reusable constructor delegate requires tracing map registration, constructor-parameter versus member-assignment mode, and the type and lifetime of compiled expressions. Helper code captures reader/resolver context, and the base class caches the delegate per record type.
rating.counterevidence: The detailed field conversions and recursive mapping are delegated to ExpressionManager. The assigned file has one clearly delineated construction choice rather than implementing those mapping rules itself.
rating.inspection_scope: Read entire assigned ObjectRecordCreator.cs, lines 1-63. Context: complete Expressions/RecordCreator.cs; ExpressionManager.cs lines 1-209 and 345-399, including constructor arguments, member assignments, and instance construction.

evidence.observation: Missing maps are created through AutoMap and added before the delegate's body is selected.

The body is compiled into Func<recordType>, making expression type correctness and captured mapping decisions part of subsequent row creation.

rating.actual_role: Builds and compiles mapped-object CSV write delegates, coordinating mapping order, custom conversions, constants, converter options, null handling, and field output.
rating.hardest_behavior: Changing generated field behavior requires distinguishing expression-construction time from later cached delegate execution while preserving mapping precedence and emitted field order. Custom conversion, constant conversion, ordinary member conversion, null records, and nested references take different paths; generated calls also affect the writer field type and output state. A meaningful change needs tracing these contracts across mapping, expression access, the cached writer, and output calls.
rating.counterevidence: Member processing is sequential and assembled from separate delegates; mapping traversal, safe nested access, conversion, and actual CSV formatting are delegated to named helpers. Existing constant and null-writing tests provide concrete behavioral examples. There is no concurrency or asynchronous lifecycle in this class.
rating.inspection_scope: Read ObjectRecordWriter.cs completely (1-121), RecordWriter.cs completely, Writing/ConstantTests.cs and Writing/WriteNullTests.cs completely. Inspected ExpressionManager.CreateGetMemberExpression (285-350), CsvWriter.WriteConvertedField (115-145), CsvWriter.CanWrite and record-type selection (685-730), and searched MemberMapCollection sorting/AddMembers locations. Did not execute tests or inspect every configuration combination.

evidence.observation: The generator may add an auto-map, flattens mapped members for ordering, and treats an empty map as an error before building any delegates.
A custom writing conversion constructs typed arguments and calls WriteField directly, then continues before the general CanWrite filter; changing order changes policy.
Constants use their runtime-type converter, while ordinary members require a configured converter and mutate merged options before embedding conversion calls in expressions.
Ordinary mapped access relies on ExpressionManager, wraps class records in a null conditional, and calls WriteConvertedField with the mapped field type. This differs from the custom-conversion path.
Per-member expression trees are compiled and combined into a later-executed action, so construction-time state and runtime writer effects must be considered separately.

rating.hardest_behavior: Keep eligibility and converter selection aligned, with specific array/dictionary/collection cases ahead of the generic enumerable fallback.
rating.counterevidence: The cases mainly form a static type-to-converter mapping; there is no collection traversal, element conversion, or evolving scan state here.
rating.inspection_scope: Full src/CsvHelper/TypeConversion/CollectionConverterFactory.cs, lines 1-172.

evidence.observation: Eligibility checks array and specific generic forms before accepting other IEnumerable-compatible types.

rating.attention_priority_reason: A focused mapping/precedence review is appropriate; numerous listed cases do not themselves imply interacting behavioral complexity.
rating.review_difficulty_reason: Review can compare CanCreate with Create and check special-case identification without following a multi-stage lifecycle.

rating.role: Production converter that gathers CSV fields into a generic collection resolved from member metadata.

rating.counterevidence: Collection construction is performed once and fields are appended sequentially. There is no persistent lifecycle or recursive algorithm in this file; reader conversion internals were not inspected.
rating.inspection_scope: Read entire assigned CollectionGenericConverter.cs, lines 1-62; no additional context.

evidence.observation: Collection and element types come from the mapped member, while named selection wins when explicitly named or when headers exist without an explicit index.

rating.actual_role: CSV enum converter supporting NameAttribute aliases, optional case-insensitive matching, ordinary enum parsing, and reverse alias formatting.

Forward and reverse mappings are intentionally not a simple bijection; fallback failure and null formatting also inherit behavior from the base converter.
rating.counterevidence: The dictionaries are populated only during construction and then read. Parsing ultimately delegates to framework enum operations; the focused enum test file supplies duplicate-name/value and case-sensitivity examples. There are no cross-record state transitions or broad orchestration responsibilities.
rating.inspection_scope: Read EnumConverter.cs completely (1-116), TypeConversion/EnumConverterTests.cs completely, and DefaultTypeConverter.cs completely. Static review only; neither target-framework branch was executed.

evidence.observation: Exact aliases, case-insensitive aliases, and reverse value-to-name formatting are represented by separate dictionaries with different key semantics.

The per-member ignore-case option selects the alias dictionary, and recognized aliases take precedence over framework parsing.
Two target-framework implementations use TryParse or Parse with catch, then delegate failures to the base converter.
Output uses the chosen reverse alias when present and otherwise uses base formatting, so accepted input aliases do not all become output spellings.

rating.hardest_behavior: Retain round-trip-oriented default formatting, explicit option precedence, culture-aware parsing, and fallback behavior for unsupported inputs.

rating.actual_role: Provider-independent DbException number matching through a cached, compiled accessor for a public integer Number property.

Reflection restricts the Number contract to a readable public instance property of the exact type, compiles a cast/property-access lambda, and maps construction exceptions to a missing accessor.

rating.actual_role: Production asynchronous multi-result reader and resource lifecycle
rating.hardest_behavior: Maintain exactly-once ordered grid consumption, schema-appropriate deserialization, and reader/command completion through buffered, single-row, deferred, and asynchronous streaming paths.

evidence.observation: Finishing the matching grid either advances/reset-consumption state or disposes the reader, invokes completion, and disposes the command.
Reads mark consumption before selecting buffered or synchronous deferred behavior, and reuse deserializers only when column hashes match.
Single-row variants combine first/default/single semantics, surplus-row reads, deserialization, and grid advancement.
Buffered and async-streaming loops guard the grid index and advance in finally, including early enumeration termination.
Disposal conditionally cancels an open reader, uses target-framework-specific disposal, then releases the command.

rating.attention_priority_reason: Changes affect resource ownership, output callbacks, and subsequent result availability across asynchronous operation boundaries.
rating.review_difficulty_reason: Review must follow state shared with another partial file, cache/schema changes, cancellation, early disposal, and different exception/cleanup paths.

rating.role: Production owner of a database reader's ordered result sets, supporting row cardinality, deferred reads, multi-mapping, and cleanup.
rating.hardest_behavior: Preserving result ownership and resource lifetime when callers buffer, defer, abandon, or fail during a read. Consumption flags, result indexes, mapping cache identities, iterator-finally advancement, completion callbacks, and async counterparts form interacting nonlocal invariants.
rating.counterevidence: The many typed public overloads mostly delegate and should not inflate the assessment. Central before/after hooks and conversion helpers make much of the behavior reviewable, but their invocation timing still differs between pathways.
rating.inspection_scope: Read entire assigned SqlMapper.GridReader.cs, lines 1-494, and entire assigned SqlMapper.GridReader.Async.cs, lines 1-314. No database providers/tests executed; MultiMapImpl and deserializer implementation internals were not inspected.

evidence.observation: OnBeforeGrid rejects disposed/already-consumed results and sets a shared consumed bit before selecting a schema-sensitive deserializer and returning a buffered or deferred sequence.
Single-row operations combine required/optional cardinality, extra-row detection, draining, and subsequent advancement; exceptions can interrupt this order.
Multi-map iterator bodies acquire grid ownership and advance from finally, so invocation and enumeration timing are semantically significant.
Deferred enumeration guards against a changed result index and advances from finally; the result index and active-consumption flag occupy the same field.
Result completion either resets state for the next result or disposes the reader before invoking callbacks and disposing the command; explicit early disposal additionally cancels an open command.

rating.hardest_behavior: Preserve lazy reader advancement and typed conversion while choosing delegates compatible with reference and value types.

rating.actual_role: Production identity and equality keys for cached queries
rating.hardest_behavior: Maintain equality/hash agreement across base, generic, and array-backed identities, including ordered mapping types and connection comparison.

rating.actual_role: Internal reference-keyed concurrent append-only micro-cache used for provider command initialization delegates.
rating.hardest_behavior: Changing insertion or reset semantics requires tracing concurrent lookup, duplicate insertion, and clearing against immutable snapshots. Publication must preserve the chain, a competing insertion must be retried, and a caller losing a duplicate-key race must receive the already-published value through its ref parameter. These are interacting temporal invariants that are not established by a single sequential execution.
rating.counterevidence: The concurrency surface is deliberately small: nodes are immutable, there is one head reference, no per-node removal, and matching is explicitly by object identity. The inspected caller tolerates independently constructing a candidate before insertion. These constraints make the proof substantially smaller than a general concurrent collection.
rating.inspection_scope: Read SqlMapper.Link.cs completely (1-63). Searched Link usages in Dapper and inspected CommandDefinition.cs 125-205, including cache reset, lookup, delegate construction, and TryAdd. No execution or exhaustive concurrency-test review.

evidence.observation: The stated contract combines reference equality and thread safety with append-only values; Clear independently exchanges the shared head.
Lookup traverses an existing chain and uses identity equality; a successful lookup returns the stored value without mutating nodes.
TryAdd snapshots the head atomically, checks duplicates, returns a competing value by ref, and publishes only if the head still matches that snapshot; retry restarts the duplicate check.
Constructor-only Key, Value, and Tail initialization is part of the immutable-chain assumption on which concurrent traversal depends.

rating.role: Production immutable stack of log-event enrichers with a mutable value-type enumerator.
rating.hardest_behavior: Preserving the empty sentinel and newest-first enumeration while allowing Reset to revisit the original immutable stack. This needs focused review of the cursor transition and empty-stack assumptions.
rating.counterevidence: There are no callbacks, external resources, or mutations of existing stack nodes. Count and enumeration state have direct local definitions.
rating.inspection_scope: Read entire assigned EnricherStack.cs, lines 1-91; no additional context.

evidence.observation: Push constructs a new node over the old stack; Count derives from the predecessor and IsEmpty depends on a missing predecessor.
Enumerator retains the initial stack separately from its advancing cursor; MoveNext stops at the sentinel, and Reset restores both cursor and current value.

limitation: Phase-one labels reused as development only; induced pairs share files and are not independent
